description: First baseline with the Phase 4 trust layer active: MiniCheck per-claim verification, weighted confidence scoring, and calibrated confidence-gated abstention (SPEC.md §3.3). NOT directly comparable to baselines/baseline.json (phase 3) on generation/judge metrics — this run's generation ran on a hosted free-tier model (OpenRouter ling-3.0-flash) rather than self-hosted qwen3:4b-instruct, forced by a local-memory ceiling (DECISIONS.md 2026-08-04/06). Retrieval metrics ARE comparable (same corpus, same retrieval pipeline, no generation involved) and are the intended regression signal.

corpus.source: arXiv LLM/RAG papers, discovered via arXiv API (scripts/seed_demo_corpus.py)

completeness.failure_cause: OpenRouter free tier's 50-requests/day cap, hit near the end of the run after 32 of the 39 full-pipeline items had already completed. GeminiProvider/OpenRouterProvider both retry 429s with exponential backoff (4 attempts), which handles per-minute limits but cannot recover from a daily cap. Per-item failure isolation (DECISIONS.md 2026-08-02) kept the run completing and aggregating from the 110 successes rather than discarding everything.
completeness.note: Every metric below carries its own `n`, so the shortfall is visible per-metric rather than hidden in a single headline count.

config.abstain_threshold_source: calibration run a04927ff-0a36-4450-87a0-df6accb0a210 (2026-08-03), fit on eval-datasets/v1/calibration.jsonl targeting >=0.90 answered-precision (SPEC.md §8.5)

latency_ms.note: per-item wall clock mixing retrieval-only items (seconds) with full-pipeline items (generation + MiniCheck verification + judge). Not a query-latency SLO number.

vs_spec_targets.note: SPEC.md §7.2 targets vs this run. Phase 4's own exit criteria are unsupported_claim_rate <= 0.05 and abstention recall >= 0.80 on the unanswerable subset.

abstention_recall_unanswerable.caveat: n=6 unanswerable items reached the full pipeline before the daily quota cut the run short (the 39-item subset contained 9). A perfect 1.0 on n=6 has a wide true interval; the calibration run (2026-08-03) independently measured 23/23 unanswerable items correctly abstaining, which is the stronger evidence for this criterion.

unsupported_claim_rate.analysis: Missed by a wide margin, and reported as measured rather than adjusted. Two contributing factors, neither of which fully excuses it: (1) MiniCheck is a strict sentence-level entailment checker — a claim that paraphrases, aggregates across two chunks, or states something only implied by the source is marked unsupported even when a human would accept it; (2) the generator here is a free-tier hosted model that was not prompt-tuned against MiniCheck's notion of support. The metric is doing its job (it surfaces genuinely weakly-grounded claims); closing the gap is generation/prompt work, not a measurement fix, and is deferred rather than papered over.

comparability.retrieval_metrics: Directly comparable to baselines/baseline.json (phase 3): same corpus, same retrieval pipeline, generation-independent. hit_rate 0.988 -> 0.988, NDCG@10 0.950 -> 0.949, MRR 0.939 -> 0.936 — all within noise, confirming the trust layer added no retrieval regression.
comparability.generation_and_judge_metrics: NOT comparable to phase 3: different generation provider (openrouter/ling-3.0-flash vs ollama/qwen3:4b-instruct). Differences in faithfulness/answer_correctness/context_* reflect the model swap at least as much as the trust layer.
comparability.abstention_metrics: NOT comparable to phase 3: phase 3 derived `abstained` from the generator's raw insufficient_context flag; phase 4 derives it from the calibrated confidence gate (a deliberate semantic change, DECISIONS.md 2026-08-03).
